*J U D G M E N T*

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
 2.

Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 15.5.2020 at about 1.45 p.m. the petitioner was riding his bike bearing registration No.KA06EP8093, from  3 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 Yediyur side towards Kunigal side, while so proceeding slowly on the left side of the said road, in front of Sericulture farm at Mallipalya village,
Kunigal town, at that point of time, the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA01AB8800,
came from Kunigal side towards Yadiyuru side without observing any traffic rules and regulations,
in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, thereby dashed against the two wheeler.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the Shri Krishna vs Ghouse Peer on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173317893/

was shifted to CHC, Kunigal, wherein, first aid treatment was taken, thereafter he was shifted to Swasthaya Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein, he was treated as an inpatient.
Further, he was shifted to Sparsha Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein, also the petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient.
The petitioner had spent Rs.6,00,000/ towards  4 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment.

4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy,
aged about 40 years, working as a labour and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
And he used to spend the said amount, for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending Vehicle bearing No.KA01 AB8800.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Kunigal Police as per Crime No.129/2020.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

sentences.text: 6. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, the respondents have appeared through their respective counsel.
The respondent No.1 has not filed the written statement.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2, has filed the written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
7. In the objection of the respondent No.2, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But, seriously disputed the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
But, not disputed about the insurance policy and it its validity from 13.12.2016 to 12.12.2019.
It is the main contention of the respondent that, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the  6 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the lorry.

It is the contention of the respondent that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle and Shri Krishna vs Ghouse Peer on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173317893/

Further, contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of the case, following issues are framed;
 *ISSUES*
 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he  had sustained grievous injuries in a motor  vehicle accident that was taken place on  15.5.2020 at about 1.45 p.m. on B.M. road,
 infront of Sericulture, Mallipalya, Kunigal  Taluk, due to the rash and negligent  7 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020  driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing  registration No.KA01AB8800 in an  actionable negligence?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the  compensation as prayed for? If so, at what  rate ? from whom?
 3) What order or award?

In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Ramesh B. as PW2.

10. On the other hand, to prove the defenses forthcoming in the objection of the respondent No.2,

Hence, the matter was set down for arguments.
11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel.
And perused the materials available on record.

12. After hearing the arguments of both the learned counsel and by scrutinizing the evidence adduced by both the parties in toto, this court proceed to answer the above issues as follows;
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3: As per final order
In connection with this issue, burden is on the petitionerKrishna, to prove that, due to the Shri Krishna vs Ghouse Peer on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173317893/

And in  9 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
14. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, has not challenged the case of the petitioner.

The respondent No.2 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
And contended that, due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the defending vehicle, accident in question, and its consequences were taken place.
But not adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.
Hence, let me to discuss the evidence available on record in order to come to the conclusion in connection with the above issue.
15. Burden is on the petitioner, to prove the above issue as per law on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.

To discharge the  10 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 burden lies on the petitionerKrishnappa/Krishna relied on his affidavit evidence, wherein, he reiterated Shri Krishna vs Ghouse Peer on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173317893/
7 the main petition averments to the effect that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle accident in question had taken place and in the said accident he sustained grievous injuries.

Among the documentary evidence Ex.P1 to Ex.P7 are the material documents in proof of the above issue.
Remaining documents as well as the evidence of PW2 are to be discussed in detail, at the time of discussion of issue No.2.

On taking birds eye view towards the above documents reflects that, on the basis of first information given by one Thimmappa, who is none other than the brother of the petitioner, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle lorry bearing registration No.KA01AB8800 alleging that, he has committed the offences punishable under  11 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 section 279 and 337 of IPC.

In connection with one day delay in giving first information is concerned, in column No.3 (c) of Ex.P1, and in the recitals of the Ex.P2, it is noted that, since the complainant was providing treatment to the injured petitioner, belated complaint was given.

17. Apart from this, in the recitals of the Ex.P1 & Ex.P2, there is a clear narration about the negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle to cause accident, consequently the petitioner sustained injuries.

In the spot mahazar marked at Ex.P3 and Ex.P4 and report of the motor vehicle inspector Ex.P5, as well as the wound certificate of the petitioner marked at Ex.P6 reveal that, after setting the criminal law in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle, the investigation officer  12 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 visited the scene of occurrence and conducted spot mahazar.

The said documents reveal about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
and as per the opinion of the inspector, alleged accident was not due to any mechanical defects and the damages noted in the said documents remained unshaken.
Added to this, as per the wound certificate, on the history of RTA the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Ultimately, the final report submitted by the investigation officer against the driver of the offending vehicle by name Gousepeer alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC, and allegation made in the column No.17 Shri Krishna vs Ghouse Peer on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173317893/
9 of the said document remained unshaken.

In the absence of contra materials and rebuttal evidence to impeach the police papers submitted by the petitioner, there is no hurdle to consider the said  13 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 document as conclusive proof in support of the case of the petitioner.

18. On the other hand, at the time of cross examination of PW1, though several questions put to this witness, nothing worthwhile is elicited to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement of the respondent No.2.
As such, the petitioner herein, had placed convincing and cogent documents in support of the above issue for consideration.

the same is unimpeached by the respondents, by questioning the recitals of police papers well in time,

In the light of the above discussions, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory and reliable evidence, to prove the above issue to the effect that, the alleged accident had  14 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 Shri Krishna vs Ghouse Peer on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173317893/

Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :

This issue is with respect to the entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

21 . Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him, in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
15 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020  Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held  that, the court has to make judicious  attempt to award compensation to the loss  suffered by the claimant.
The compensation  should not be assessed conservatively.
On  the other hand, compensation should also  not be endeavouring to secure some  uniformity and consistency.

The object of  awarding compensation is to make good the  loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as Shri Krishna vs Ghouse Peer on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173317893/
11  far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable  and equitable manner."

For having taken the note of the nature of the injuries sustained by him, and by keeping in mind about his sufferings during the said period of treatment, in connection with the grievous injuries, and also mode of treatment given to him.

about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period.

31. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition,

LIABILITY:
 38.
As regards the liability is concerned, in the case on hand, accident has not been seriously disputed by the other side.

And the evidence given  28 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 by the petitioner that, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle Lorry bearing registration No.KA01AB8800, remained unshaken.
The assertion of the petitioner that, the insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of the accident, has not been denied by the respondent No.2.
As per the records policy was valid from 11.10.2019 to 10.10.2020.
Accident was occurred on 15.5.2020.

The policy furnished by the respondent No.2 also speaks about the existence of policy of the offending Shri Krishna vs Ghouse Peer on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173317893/
21 vehicle as on the date of the accident.
Further, the respondent No.2 has failed to prove that, due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, alleged accident had taken place.

Since as on the date of the accident, insurance policy was valid, both the respondents No.1 and 2, being the owner and the insurance company of the offending vehicle  29 SCCH-18 MVC 3837/2020 respectively, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
39 . However, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2, is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
 40.

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

Consequently, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,00,485/ (Rupees fourteen lakhs four hundred and eighty five only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.

Expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
Draw award accordingly.
